results.title: LLM-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning for Long-Term User Satisfaction in Interactive Recommendation
results.summary: Interactive recommender systems can dynamically adapt to user feedback, but often suffer from content homogeneity and filter bubble effects due to overfitting short-term user preferences. While recent efforts aim to improve content diversity, they predominantly operate in static or one-shot settings, neglecting the long-term evolution of user interests. Reinforcement learning provides a principled framework for optimizing long-term user satisfaction by modeling sequential decision-making processes. However, its application in recommendation is hindered by sparse, long-tailed user-item interactions and limited semantic planning capabilities. In this work, we propose LLM-Enhanced Reinforcement Learning (LERL), a novel hierarchical recommendation framework that integrates the semantic planning power of LLM with the fine-grained adaptability of RL. LERL consists of a high-level LLM-based planner that selects semantically diverse content categories, and a low-level RL policy that recommends personalized items within the selected semantic space. This hierarchical design narrows the action space, enhances planning efficiency, and mitigates overexposure to redundant content. Extensive experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that LERL significantly improves long-term user satisfaction when compared with state-of-the-art baselines. The implementation of LERL is available at https://github.com/1163710212/LERL.

results.title: G-CoS: An Interpretable Gain-Cost Framework for User Satisfaction Estimation in Generative Information Retrieval
results.summary: User satisfaction serves as a key indicator of search experience in Generative Information Retrieval (GenIR) systems, and its accurate estimation is essential for system optimization. Extensive research in traditional IR has established interaction signals (e.g., dwell time, clicks, query reformulations) as reliable indicators of user satisfaction. However, prevailing approaches for satisfaction estimation in GenIR (e.g., LLM-as-a-judge) primarily rely on textual content and fail to account for user interactions during the search process. In this work, empirical analysis of real-world data shows that user satisfaction correlates negatively with interaction signals reflecting interaction cost, and positively with response quality. Building on these findings, we propose the Gain-aware Cost-sensitive Satisfaction estimator (G-CoS), an interpretable gain-cost framework for user satisfaction estimation in GenIR. G-CoS models user satisfaction as a dynamic trade-off between Response Quality and multidimensional Interaction Cost. Experimental results demonstrate that G-CoS outperforms LLM-as-a-judge methods, interaction sequence models, as well as machine learning models using the same gain and cost features. Moreover, the learned parameters reveal interpretable associations between gain-cost dynamics and user satisfaction. This work contributes an interpretable framework for user satisfaction estimation and offers insights for GenIR system optimization.

results.title: Design and optimization of an LLM-powered digital art co-creation platform
results.summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly embedded into creative workflows, yet production-grade tools still struggle with prompt clarity, controllability, provenance, and evaluation. This paper presents the design and optimization of a digital-art co-creation platform that couples an LLM planning layer with controllable text-to-image (T2I) diffusion back-ends and a visual-language (VL) evaluator. The architecture integrates a Prompt Studio with guardrails, multicondition control (e.g., edges, depth, segmentation), and content provenance via C2PA-compatible metadata. We report prototype experiments on a mixed set of illustrative prompts, showing higher prompt adherence and user satisfaction, and lower iteration time, versus a baseline workflow. We also discuss ethical and practical concerns, including watermarking and data privacy.

results.title: LLM-Enabled User Semantic Driven Coordinated Scheduling Framework for PV–Storage–Charging Microgrids
results.summary: The complex multi-objective coupling characteristics inherent to photovoltaic (PV)-storage-charging microgrids present unprecedented challenges for dynamic energy scheduling. Existing reinforcement learning methods often exhibit limitations in modeling subjective user heterogeneity and algorithm adaptivity. This paper proposes a Large Language Model (LLM)-enhanced Proximal Policy Optimization (LLM-PPO) framework to address the aforementioned issues. The proposed method integrates the semantic parsing capability of LLMs with the continuous control capability of PPO. Specifically, the LLM-driven module transcribes qualitative user requirements into structured multi-dimensional semantic vectors, while a dynamic reward engine adaptively modulates penalty coefficients based on these individual semantic features— greatly enhancing the policy's preference-awareness and multi-objective coordination. Simulation results demonstrate that LLM-PPO improves the convergence reward plateau by 20%, enhances electric vehicle (EV) satisfaction by 27%, and simultaneously decreases grid security penalties by 9%. Furthermore, the proposed framework also exhibits superior peak-shaving efficacy and scheduling robustness against daily operational stochasticity.

results.title: Development of a Human–Computer Interaction System and Machine Learning-based User Satisfaction Prediction
results.summary: Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) has become an important research area in modern society. However, traditional interaction platforms often face problems such as limited adaptability, low interactivity, and lack of personalized responses, which reduce user engagement and learning efficiency. With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and large language models (LLMs), it is now possible to design more intelligent and responsive digital systems. This study presents the development of an intelligent HCI system that integrates LLM-based dialogue generation and digital human technologies for interactive learning. The system enables real-time conversation, scene-based teaching, and automatic evaluation to improve communication. To assess its effectiveness, a questionnaire survey was conducted in more than ten primary schools, and the collected data were analyzed using six machine learning models to predict user satisfaction. Among them, the Support Vector Machine (SVM) achieved the highest accuracy (0.8108) and F1-score (0.8111). The results indicate that combining intelligent dialogue systems with machine learning-based satisfaction prediction can effectively enhance user experience and optimize adaptive interactions.
